title: Brutal King Hunt me
reviewNotes: All 21 saved states and captions reviewed. This is a crowded middlegame king hunt with White queen, two rooks, both bishops, a knight and numerous pawns, versus Black queen, rook, two bishops, knight and pawns. Qh3+/Kxh3/Bxf3, the Nf2 overload and final rook mate do not include a worked endgame phase. Retained in the full searchable channel archive outside the endgame-study scope.
transcript: Imagine you're playing black here. After a long and hard-fought game, you find yourself in a lost position. But white has eight extra points of material and it's going to go on to win this game. But let me tell you this, the game is not over and you have not lost until you're either checkmated or the words I resign in your mouth. So, it's your move. What do you do? If you've seen any of my videos, you know that the solution [music] is going to be something stunning. And the first move that you should play here as black is the majestic queen H3 check. A full queen sacrifice, but that forces white to take this queen. But if we rush and play something like rook H8, actually the king finds shelter on G4 and any follow-up checks are just going to result in a drawn position. So after king H3, you need to be patient and play the calm, cool and collected bishop takes F3. And we are setting up a net around this king. And now rook H8 is a checkmate threat. White can [music] just stop the checkmate threat with bishop H4. And it doesn't seem like we have a followup, but I'm not showing you this to show you how to draw this game. [music] You want to win and you can with the beautiful knight f2 check. A move that sets the white king in a checkmate if it wasn't for the fact that of course the knight can be taken for free. But you see this bishop was trying to stop two checkmate threats at the same time. And now rook h8 forces the bishop back and rook to h4 is a beautiful checkmate.
